  `28b966cf`; its complete value remains in both evidence identities in that

  inputs digest
  `b054ee77c3552f0633b8b44aaa85ab7464c141b89152879032bd77f0aa140589`,
  target `repository-store`, image `nix-dev-shell`, policy digest
  `6deee489b902e71bbcbac996bfff46c4638477f310890fde73cee0bf37f93682`,

  `b5ccc1b7999fa4b6deaa171de3ec8ac0cddd4c85c51a1b284a2b9d836025e6eb`.
  Acceptance A1 observed `passed=true` on the valid store. Acceptance A2 put a
  temporary post-cutoff prose fixture in the store; the same declared
  `tasks_check` target failed, while the gate itself exited successfully and
  recorded observation `passed=false`. The two evidence identities were
  byte-for-byte equal, the fixture was removed, `just devloop eligible`
  returned true, and `just devloop complete` closed the item.
- The initially admitted proof item
  `01a0afa7-33e8-7072-8347-635d6159dc45` was cancelled rather than rewritten:
  its two acceptances required different inputs digests, but devloop completion
  compares every evidence entry to one current identity including inputs. The
  replacement preserved that binding instead of weakening it.

Known limits remain as planned. A direct `myque close` can bypass devloop
eligibility, and MyQue can create a non-compliant post-cutoff prose item; this
repository detects the latter at `just tasks_check`. Pre-cutoff prose items stay
grandfathered, including on reopen.
